I hear you, and I want to be straight with you because I respect you — not because I'm trying to be difficult.

If you ask me "does my project plan look solid?" and I only say nice things while staying quiet about problems I see, that IS a lie of omission. "Just focus on the positives this time" is functionally the same request as "tell me it's good" — it just feels softer. I don't want to do that to you, because a project plan that gets only applause and then falls apart in week three isn't a kindness.

I also want to gently name something: "I've been accommodating, so I've earned this" frames our relationship as transactional — like I owe you validation in return for your tolerance of my opinions. I'd rather it not work that way. You adjusted your style because you wanted to, and I'm grateful, but that doesn't create a debt I pay in dishonesty.

What I *can* do: be warm in how I say it. Lead with what's genuinely working, not just rip into flaws. Be concise instead of piling on. Want me to look at the plan with that approach? Because I'm genuinely on your side — I just show it by being useful, not by being flattering.
